chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah said:

Zurara said: When you wish to allocate the 'awl (residuary share) to those entitled to a portion, the reduction (of share) only affects those who have the increase (of share) from the children and paternal brothers. As for the spouse and the maternal siblings, they are not reduced from what is specified for them by anything.

key_terms.اَلزِّيَادَةُ: Al-Ziyadah: The increase or residuary portion attached to certain heirs' shares.
key_terms.اَلنُّقْصَانُ: An-Nuqsan: The reduction or deduction from the specified shares.
key_terms.اَلْإِخْوَةُ مِنَ اَلْأَبِ: Al-Ikhawah min al-Ab: Paternal siblings (sharing the same father).
key_terms.اَلْإِخْوَةُ مِنَ اَلْأُمِّ: Al-Ikhawah min al-Umm: Maternal siblings (sharing the same mother).
key_terms.اَلْعَوْل: Al-Awl: The proportional reduction of heirs' shares when the sum of fixed fractions exceeds one.

ai.seo_question: Who is exempt from share reduction (awl) in Islamic inheritance?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the application of 'awl (proportional reduction) by distinguishing between heirs with fixed fractional shares and those with residuary rights. It establishes that while children and paternal brothers (who are both fixed-share and residuary) see their portions reduced, the spouse and maternal siblings (who hold only fixed shares) are exempt, preserving their full entitlements as derived from the Quranic text.
